title: Which processes belong to a setup stage, whether a recorded process is still the one that was started, who may take over a lease, and when a stage that runs long enough to be stopped is stopped
description: A stage runs as a detached process tree. When it is stopped (time cap, cancel, a restart that finds it vanished) the whole tree must end on every platform, including processes whose parent has already exited (on Windows a tree is only a chain of recorded parent ids and a child of an exited parent is no longer reachable from the root). So the supervisor samples the process table while the stage runs, keeps the `{pid, startMs}` of every process of the tree in `<stage>.tree.json`, and stops exactly those that are still there with the same start time (a reused pid has another start time and is never touched). A lease or an in-flight record names a process by `{pid, startMs}` for the same reason. The cap of a stage is a soft cap: past it the stage keeps running while the counters in its log keep changing (`progressPatterns`), up to the stage-specific multiplier or the default `hardCapMultiplier` times the soft cap, and is stopped as stalled as soon as no counter changed for `stallMilliseconds`. Independent of the cap, a stage whose output shows nothing new for `stallStopMilliseconds` is stopped and tried again at once without counting as a failure: progress is a change in WHAT is being worked on or a growing work counter, never elapsed time in any spelling. Output is not the only sign of life: while the processes of the tree (and every recorded member) spend at least `livenessCpuMilliseconds` of processor time between two samples, or a new process joins the tree, the stage is alive and the stall clock restarts (a silent `rustc` compile is not stalled); the hard cap still bounds it. A process that other agents use (`spare`, a resident service) and everything below it is never part of a kill plan. A line is new when it differs from every earlier line of the run after every elapsed-time spelling named by `normalisePatterns` is replaced by `#` (seconds and minutes with a unit, clocks, ISO stamps, JSON members named like elapsed, waited, since, duration or ending in Ms, any JSON member holding a fractional number, epoch milliseconds, every `[repo leases]` report line of the background lease sweep, whose retired counts differ from sweep to sweep and are not the work of the stage); a counter such as `1957 of 2927` or the suffix of a resource such as `javascript-selected-payload:48022` is not normalised away, so it counts as progress; at most `stallSeenMaximum` distinct lines are remembered. A stage that waits on a named holder (a line matching `holderWaitPatterns`) for `holderWaitRestartMilliseconds` while a declared semantics source (`semanticsSources`: a JSON file and a pointer to the number or stamp that says what another process would accept from the stage, such as the revision of the selected generation exchange and the stamp of the persisted project record) differs from the value it had when the stage started (looked at every `codeCheckMilliseconds`) is stopped and started again at once, which may know that the holder is dead. The edit of any other file does not stop a stage: it runs on the code it loaded, its results are sealed under that loaded identity, and the next stage start loads the new code

holderNamedPatterns: Process (?<pid>\d+) \((?<command>.*)\) holds the dependency store since (?<since>\S+?)(?: and has not renewed its registration for (?<silent>\d+) s, so it may be blocked)?; waiting for it \((?<seconds>\d+) s of at most (?<limit>\d+) s\)

Der Prozess (?<pid>\d+) \((?<command>.*)\) hält den Abhängigkeitsspeicher seit (?<since>\S+?)(?: und hat seine Anmeldung seit (?<silent>\d+) s nicht erneuert, er ist womöglich blockiert)?; es wird darauf gewartet \((?<seconds>\d+) s von höchstens (?<limit>\d+) s\)
stepLinePatterns: ^Reading the project graph slice \((?<done>\d+) s, (?:beyond the expected|expected) (?<bound>\d+) s\): (?<step>.+? / .+?)\.$
^Lese den Projektgraph-Ausschnitt \((?<done>\d+) s, (?:über den erwarteten|erwartet) (?<bound>\d+) s\): (?<step>.+? / .+?)\.$

Tree.description: `<directory>/<stage>.tree.json`: the root of the stage and every process seen below it, replaced atomically at each sample.

StallCase.description: Rounds of the last log lines of one stage run, in order, and whether each round showed anything new.

HolderCase.description: Rounds of the last log lines of one stage run with the milliseconds since the stage started and whether a file of the code roots was modified after the start; `waitingMs` is how long a named holder has been waited for at the end of each round (0 when no round line names a holder) and `restart` whether the stage is stopped to start again with the new code.

CpuCase.description: `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,rss=,time=` text, the root and the extra pids of a stage, the processor time of its tree in ms, and the same of the sample before with the verdict whether the stage is alive between them.
